reconfigure.title: {model}
reconfigure.description: How this model should speak a reply that is still being written.

data_description.stream_mode: Automatic lets the app decide for each reply, from what it has measured about this model on its own host: spoken as it is written when the model keeps ahead of its audio, held back just long enough when it does not, and rendered whole while the model is still unmeasured. Buffered renders the whole reply before any of it plays — the longest wait, and it never stalls. Every model starts buffered; switch to automatic once the real-time factor sensor has a figure.

abort.model_comes_from_the_server: Models are not added here. Download one in the Cortex TTS app and it appears on this page by itself.
abort.reconfigure_successful: Saved. It applies to the next reply.

options.auto: Automatic — the app paces each reply
options.buffered: Buffered — render it all, then play

list_voices.name: List voices
list_voices.description: Return every voice the configured Cortex TTS servers offer, with the id `tts.speak` needs. Home Assistant lists voices only to the dashboard, so this is how an automation, a template or an agent finds one.

entity_id.name: Entity
entity_id.description: Only the voices of the model this entity speaks with. Omit it for every voice on every server.
